name: Guns N' Roses
description:
'''Guns N' Roses'''{{efn|Also stylized as '''Guns 'N' Roses''', and often abbreviated as '''GNR'''}} is an American [[hard rock]] band formed in [[Los Angeles]], California, in March 1985 by [[Axl Rose]], [[Izzy Stradlin]], [[Tracii Guns]], and others from [[L.A. Guns]] and [[Hollywood Rose]]. The classic lineup, Rose (vocals), [[Slash (musician)|Slash]] (lead guitar), Stradlin (rhythm guitar), [[Duff McKagan]] (bass), and [[Steven Adler]] (drums), was finalized in June 1985. After signing with [[Geffen Records]] in 1986, the band released its debut album ''[[Appetite for Destruction]]'' (1987). Initially slow to sell, it broke through with the "[[Welcome to the Jungle]]" music video and went on to sell more than 30 million copies worldwide, becoming the [[List of best-selling albums in the United States|best-selling debut album]] in the U.S. It produced three ''Billboard'' [[Billboard Hot 100|Hot 100]] top-ten singles: "Welcome to the Jungle", "[[Paradise City]]", and the band's only number-one, "[[Sweet Child o' Mine]]". The follow-up, ''[[G N' R Lies]]'' (1988), reached number two and featured the top-five single "[[Patience (Guns N' Roses song)|Patience]]".

Adler was fired in 1990 and replaced by [[Matt Sorum]]. The twin albums ''[[Use Your Illusion I]]'' and ''[[Use Your Illusion II|II]]'' (1991) debuted at numbers two and one on the ''Billboard'' 200 and sold a combined 35 million copies worldwide. The ''Illusion'' albums featured [[List of most expensive music videos|high-budget music videos]], including "[[November Rain]]", which reached number three on the ''Billboard'' Hot 100 and later became the first 1990s music video to reach [[List of most-viewed YouTube videos#Billion-View Club|one billion]] [[YouTube]] views. The subsequent [[Use Your Illusion Tour]] (1991–93) was marked by the [[Riverport Riot]] and other incidents; Stradlin left mid-tour and was replaced by [[Gilby Clarke]], who appeared on the punk covers album ''[["The Spaghetti Incident?"]]'' (1993). Clarke was later replaced by [[Paul Tobias]], whose presence contributed to friction that led Slash, Sorum and McKagan to leave between 1996 and 1997. By 1998, only Rose and keyboardist [[Dizzy Reed]] remained from the ''Illusion'' era.

Rose rebuilt the band with a rotating cast that included [[Brain (musician)|Brain]], [[Buckethead]], [[Frank Ferrer]], [[Robin Finck]], [[Richard Fortus]], [[Josh Freese]], [[Chris Pitman]], Reed, [[Tommy Stinson]], [[Ron "Bumblefoot" Thal]], and Tobias. The long-delayed ''[[Chinese Democracy]]'' (2008), reportedly the [[List of most expensive albums|most expensive album]] ever made at $13 million, debuted at number three but undersold expectations and was banned in China. The [[Chinese Democracy Tour]] (2001-2011) included cancelled dates and riots. After years of public feuding, Slash and McKagan rejoined the band in 2016 for the [[Not in This Lifetime... Tour]], which grossed $563.3 million and ranked as the [[List of highest-grossing concert tours|second-highest-grossing concert tour]] at the time. Since the reunion, the band has released deluxe editions of ''[[Appetite for Destruction#Remastered version|Appetite for Destruction]]'' (2018) and ''[[Use Your Illusion#Remastered box set|Use Your Illusion]]'' (2022), a remastered ''[[Live Era '87–'93]]'' (2025), and new singles "[[Absurd (song)|Absurd]]", "[[Hard Skool]]" (2021),  "[[Perhaps (song)|Perhaps]]" (2023), "[[Nothin' (Guns N' Roses song)|Nothin']]" and "[[Atlas (Guns N' Roses song)|Atlas]]" (2025). The current lineup is Rose, Slash, McKagan, rhythm guitarist Fortus, drummer [[Isaac Carpenter (drummer)|Isaac Carpenter]], and keyboardists Reed and [[Melissa Reese]].

Guns N' Roses has sold more than [[List of best-selling music artists|100 million records worldwide]]. ''[[Greatest Hits (Guns N' Roses album)|Greatest Hits]]'' (2004) is one of the [[Billboard 200#Most weeks on the chart|longest-charting albums]] in the history of the ''Billboard'' 200. Their early sound fused [[punk rock|punk]], [[blues rock|blues]], hard rock, and [[Heavy metal music|metal]]; the ''Illusion'' albums added [[progressive rock|progressive]] and [[art rock]] elements, and ''Chinese Democracy'' incorporated [[industrial rock|industrial]] and [[electronic music|electronic]] textures. ''Appetite for Destruction'' is credited with helping end the late-1980s [[glam metal]] craze and was inducted into the [[Grammy Hall of Fame]] in 2024. The band was inducted into the [[Rock and Roll Hall of Fame]] in 2012, though Rose declined to attend. Incidents including Rose's 1987 arrest in Atlanta, the deaths of two fans at the 1988 [[Monsters of Rock]] festival, and multiple riots earned the band the label "the most dangerous band in the world". Controversies arose over lyrics (notably "[[One in a Million (Guns N' Roses song)|One in a Million]]"), a hidden [[Charles Manson]] cover on ''"The Spaghetti Incident?"'', chronic late concert starts and [[List of longest gaps between studio albums#10–19 years|long gaps between albums]].
